title: Surinam Toad Babies Burst Out of Mom's Back Skin
subject: Surinam toad

scenes.text: This toad grows its babies inside her own back.
The male presses 60 to 100 fertilized eggs onto the female's back.
Within a day, her skin swells around each egg, making a pocket.
The babies develop in those pockets for about four months.
Then fully formed toadlets push through her skin and swim away.
She sheds her skin and gets ready to do it again.

description:
A female Surinam toad grows her babies inside pockets in her back skin.
After about four months, fully formed toadlets push their way out.
Would you want to see it happen?
first_comment: Egg counts differ by source, from about 60 to 100. What weird parent should we cover next?
